newsitem.title: INDIA: FOCUS - India's VSNL maps out GDR launch.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - India's VSNL maps out GDR launch.

text.p: India's state-run overseas telecommunications monopoly, Videsh Sanchar Nigam Ltd (VSNL), on Thursday mapped out the launch for its long-awaited jumbo issue of Global Depositary Receipts (GDRs), company officials said.

The issue, worth $567 million at current market prices, consists of a maximum of 18.9 million shares represented by 37.8 million GDRs, and is to be listed on the London Stock Exchange, and priced sometime in the last week of March.
VSNL also plans a local issue of 600,000 shares to retail investors soon after the GDR, to be followed by an issue of shares to employees.
Taken together, the issues will reduce the size of the Indian government's holding in VSNL from 82.02 percent at present to 65 percent of the expanded equity, Gokak said.
"We expect the GDR to be large and liquid," VSNL Chairman and Managing Director Brijendra Syngal told a news conference.

Shares of VSNL, which has a monopoly on international telecommunications and Internet access services in India, closed 38 rupees up, at 1,075 rupees, on the Bombay Stock Exchange. The market had closed before the announcement was made.
Roadshows will begin on Monday in Hong Kong, led by senior officials of India's industry, finance, and telecommunications ministries.

"VSNL is a large good issue coming at a time when people are overweight on India, and they can use it as a proxy for exposure to India," said Roddy Sale, international capital markets director at Jardine Fleming India Securities, one of the global coordinators of the issue.

But it has run into snags in the past. Adverse market conditions and bureaucratic delays have combined to delay the GDR issue several times. This is VSNL's third launch attempt in two years after two unsuccessful attempts in 1994.

VSNL is pinning its hopes on this launch, and Finance Minister P.Chidambaram gave Indian share markets a massive boost with an investor friendly, pro-growth 1997/98 (April-March) budget on February 28.

"The GDR is also important to our customers in terms of the range and quality of services we can provide, and since the world's eyes will be on us, it is important to the country and to all Indian company paper," Syngal said.
A company pamphlet said a maximum of 30 million GDRs will be offered by VSNL, and a maximum of 7.8 million GDRs by the state, which is the principal shareholder.
The issue will be priced sometime around the end of March, a top Indian official said.
"The decision on the price will be taken in the last week of March, probably around March 25," said A.V. Gokak, the highest-ranking civil servant in the telecommunications department.
"There will be an issue of 600,000 shares to domestic retail investors shortly after the GDR issue and there will also be a share issue to employees," Syngal said, but gave no details.
"The details of the actual offer will be decided only after the GDR issue," Syngal added.

Officials declined to give any pricing details. "The price will be determined only on the completion of bookbuilding, and will be market-driven, and we are optimistic," Gokak said in reply to a question on the expected price.
VSNL will use the funds raised by the issue to expand capacity, invest in infrastructure, improve the quality of its services and add new services, Gokak added.
VSNL earnings have grown 34 percent annually during the years from 1991 to 1996, with net income on average growing at 28.9 percent over the same period.
During the first half of financial 1996/97 (April-March), VSNL's net profit was 2.65 billion rupees as compared to 1.66 billion in the corresponding period the previous year.

The joint global coordinators to the issue are Dresdner Kleinwort Benson, Jardine Fleming and Salomon Brothers, with Cazenove & Co., HSBC James Capel, Merrill Lynch and UBS the co-lead managers. BZW, CS First Boston, ING Barings, Lehman Brothers, Morgan Stanley and Peregrine will be co-managers.
SBI Capital Markets is the domestic advisor to the company.
